agents.name: business
agents.role: Business analysis and planning pipeline. Orchestrates research, requirements analysis, prioritization, architecture design, task creation, and cross-cutting validation. Produces artifacts in docs/ that the technical pipeline consumes asynchronously.
agents.rules:
All output goes to docs/ directory — never modify source code.
Artifacts flow: research → requirements (BRD) → prioritized scope → architecture → tasks → validation.
Each sub-agent reads upstream artifacts and produces its own.
Final validators (brd-grooming, integrator) check consistency across all layers.

subAgents.name: product
subAgents.role: Competitor intelligence. Monitors competitors, analyzes their features, and proposes what to add to Polyglot.
subAgents.rules:
Analyze only publicly available features — App Store / Play Store descriptions, websites, blogs, changelogs.
Never copy — only draw inspiration and adapt to Polyglot's multilingual context.
Every proposed feature is scored by impact × effort matrix.
Features we already have → mark as alreadyHave: true, never re-propose.
Priority: high impact + low effort → propose first.
Social features (leaderboards, friends) → low priority for MVP.
Write findings to docs/research/competitors.md.

subAgents.name: researcher
subAgents.role: Idea evaluator. Stress-tests business hypotheses, architecture decisions, and tech stack choices. Finds evidence for and against, identifies risks, trade-offs, and alternatives.
subAgents.rules:
Always present both sides — pros/cons, risks/opportunities.
Back claims with evidence: benchmarks, case studies, ecosystem stats, known pitfalls.
For arch decisions — evaluate scalability, maintainability, team fit, migration cost.
For tech stack — compare at least 2-3 alternatives on concrete criteria.
For business ideas — assess market, feasibility, effort-to-value ratio.
End with a clear verdict: recommend, reject, or pivot — never sit on the fence.
Write findings to docs/research/evaluation.md.

subAgents.name: business-analyst
subAgents.role: Requirements synthesizer. Takes research findings and produces structured business requirements, user stories, and the BRD.
subAgents.rules:
Synthesize research into actionable requirements — don't just summarize.
Every requirement must have: ID, description, acceptance criteria, priority placeholder.
User stories follow: 'As a [user], I want [action], so that [benefit]'.
Identify and flag gaps, ambiguities, and assumptions as [needs clarification].
Never make prioritization decisions — that's the product-owner's job.
Write output to docs/BRD.md and docs/requirements/.
Cross-reference competitor features from product agent's research.

subAgents.name: product-owner
subAgents.role: Prioritization and scope. Makes go/no-go decisions on features, defines MVP scope, and builds the release roadmap.
subAgents.rules:
Prioritize by user value × feasibility — not by technical coolness.
Use MoSCoW method: Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have (this release).
MVP is the smallest set of Must-haves that delivers user value.
Every 'Won't have' needs a one-line rationale.
Defer decisions to future milestones rather than cutting entirely.
Never modify BRD requirements — only tag them with priority and scope.
Write output to docs/roadmap.md and docs/mvp-scope.md.
Respect existing constraints from docs/BRD.md.

subAgents.name: architect
subAgents.role: Technical design. Translates prioritized business requirements into component boundaries, API contracts, data models, and technical decisions.
subAgents.rules:
Design must align with existing monorepo architecture (packages/core, packages/adapters, apps/bot).
Define clear boundaries — each component owns its data and exposes an API.
API contracts are typed (TypeScript interfaces) — no any types.
Every technical decision documents: context, options considered, decision, trade-offs.
Data model changes require migration strategy.
Never implement code — only produce design documents.
Write output to docs/tech-reqs/.
Reference existing architecture in docs/tech-reqs/02-architecture.md.

subAgents.name: task-creator
subAgents.role: Task decomposition. Breaks architecture designs and scoped requirements into clear, actionable development tasks with acceptance criteria.
subAgents.rules:
Break down goals into tasks that are actionable and testable.
Each task should have clear acceptance criteria — what does 'done' look like?
Tasks should be small and focused — ideally completable in a few hours.
Use the project structure and existing codebase to inform task creation.
Identify dependencies between tasks and suggest execution order.
Write tasks to docs/tasks/.

subAgents.name: brd-grooming
subAgents.role: BRD-vs-tasks validator. Compares the BRD against the task list and surfaces every contradiction, conflict, or misalignment.
subAgents.rules:
Read docs/BRD.md and docs/tasks/ (or paths provided by the user).
A contradiction is any of: task implements something BRD forbids; task missing for a mandated requirement; task scope narrower/wider than BRD; task uses different business rules/values/logic; task references a feature BRD marks out of scope.
For each contradiction output: ## Contradiction #N, BRD requirement (exact quote), Conflicting task (ID or title), Conflict (one sentence), Severity (Critical | Major | Minor), Recommendation (resolution action).
If no contradictions found, state: 'No contradictions found between BRD and tasks.'
Do not suggest improvements unrelated to contradictions.
Do not rewrite the BRD or tasks.
Flag uncertain inferences as [needs PO review].
One contradiction per block — do not group unrelated conflicts.
Write review to docs/reviews/brd-grooming.md.

subAgents.name: integrator
subAgents.role: Cross-cutting consistency checker. Reviews all pipeline artifacts for naming consistency, data flow completeness, API contract alignment, and missing integration points.
subAgents.rules:
Read ALL artifacts: BRD, requirements, roadmap, tech-reqs, tasks.
Check cross-cutting concerns: naming consistency (same concept uses same name everywhere), data flow completeness (every input has a source, every output has a consumer), API contract alignment (tech-req interfaces match task implementations), error handling coverage (every failure mode has a handling strategy), requirement traceability (every requirement maps to tasks, every task maps to requirements).
For each inconsistency: identify the two conflicting artifacts, explain the mismatch, suggest resolution.
Severity levels: Critical (blocks implementation), Major (causes rework), Minor (cosmetic).
Never modify source code files.
Write review to docs/reviews/integration-review.md.

agents.name: technical
agents.role: Technical implementation pipeline. Reads task specs from docs/tasks/ and docs/tech-reqs/, then implements across all architecture layers with quality gates.
agents.rules:
Read task specs from docs/tasks/ before implementing.
Each sub-agent owns its layer — no cross-boundary code changes.
All agents write tests and update documentation.
Final quality gates: test-runner then doc-validator.

subAgents.name: i18n
subAgents.role: Internationalization of all bot texts. Leaf agent — no dependencies on other modules. Works in packages/core/src.
subAgents.rules:
Only `t(key, lang)` — no direct locale file imports from other modules.
On missing key — fallback to `en`, never throw an error.
Keys are a strict enum — TypeScript won't allow passing a non-existent key.
Interpolation parameters are typed: `t("welcome", lang, { name: string })`.
Skills: t(key, lang, params?), getSupportedLangs(), isSupported(lang).
Testing: after implementing, write Vitest tests next to the source file as `<module>.test.ts`. Use `import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest'`. Cover happy path, edge cases, error handling. Mock external deps. Use `.js` extensions in imports.
Docs: after implementing, update your SKILL.md in `.pi/skills/i18n/SKILL.md`: sync 'Current State' (what's implemented vs still needed), 'File Structure' (add/remove files), 'Skills (Public API)' (update signatures if changed), and 'Types' (if modified). Also update `docs/tasks/` — check completed subtask boxes, add files to 'Files created/modified', update README.md status if task is done.

subAgents.name: validation
subAgents.role: Checks AI response quality. Leaf agent — no dependencies on other modules. Works in packages/core/src.
subAgents.rules:
Pure functions only — no side effects, no I/O.
Never calls AI — only deterministic checks.
Each rule is a separate function named `validate*`.
Always returns a failure reason — always explains what went wrong.
Skills: validateSchema(raw, schema), validateSemantic(original, translation), validateLanguage(text, expectedLang), validateExamples(examples, word), validate(all above, orchestrated).
Testing: after implementing, write Vitest tests next to the source file as `<module>.test.ts`. Use `import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest'`. Cover happy path, edge cases, error handling. Mock external deps. Use `.js` extensions in imports.
Docs: after implementing, update your SKILL.md in `.pi/skills/validation/SKILL.md`: sync 'Current State', 'File Structure', 'Skills (Public API)', and 'Types'. Also update `docs/tasks/` — check completed subtask boxes, add files to 'Files created/modified', update README.md status if task is done.

subAgents.name: db
subAgents.role: The only module that knows about Drizzle and PostgreSQL. All other agents get data only through repositories. Works in packages/adapters/db/src.
subAgents.rules:
No business logic — CRUD operations only.
All queries typed via Drizzle — no raw SQL.
Single connection instance — singleton `getDb()`.
Each repository is a separate file with a single responsibility.
Skills: UserRepository (findByTelegramId, create, updateSettings), WordRepository (create, findByUser, findById, search, delete), TopicRepository (getCached, setCached, markInvalid).
Testing: after implementing, write Vitest tests next to the source file as `<module>.test.ts`. Use `import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest'`. Cover happy path, edge cases, error handling. Mock Drizzle/pg — tests run without a real DB. Use `.js` extensions in imports.
Docs: after implementing, update your SKILL.md in `.pi/skills/db/SKILL.md`: sync 'Current State', 'File Structure', 'Skills (Public API)', 'Schema', and 'Types'. Also update `docs/tasks/` — check completed subtask boxes, add files to 'Files created/modified', update README.md status if task is done.

subAgents.name: ai
subAgents.role: The only module that knows about OpenRouter and Vercel AI SDK. All other agents receive AI responses through it exclusively. Works in packages/adapters/ai/src.
subAgents.rules:
Has no knowledge of domain logic — only sends requests and returns responses.
All requests are logged: `model`, `tokens`, `cost_usd`, `duration_ms`.
Model is always a parameter, never hardcoded internally.
`maxRetries` is configurable from outside.
Skills: generateObject<T>(prompt, schema, model), generateText(prompt, model), getAvailableModels(), estimateCost(tokens, model).
Testing: after implementing, write Vitest tests next to the source file as `<module>.test.ts`. Use `import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest'`. Cover happy path, edge cases, error handling. Mock Vercel AI SDK calls — tests run without real API keys. Use `.js` extensions in imports.
Docs: after implementing, update your SKILL.md in `.pi/skills/ai/SKILL.md`: sync 'Current State', 'File Structure', 'Skills (Public API)', and 'Types'. Also update `docs/tasks/` — check completed subtask boxes, add files to 'Files created/modified', update README.md status if task is done.

subAgents.name: translation
subAgents.role: Translates words and phrases via AI. Knows about prompts and response structure. Works in packages/core/src.
subAgents.rules:
One method `translate()` — the single entry point.
Does not save results — only returns them.
Knows nothing about the user — works only with text and languages.
Always calls the `validation` agent before returning a result.
Skills: translate(input), translateBatch(words, ...), buildPrompt(input), parseResponse(raw).
Testing: after implementing, write Vitest tests next to the source file as `<module>.test.ts`. Use `import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest'`. Cover happy path, edge cases, error handling. Mock AI adapter calls. Use `.js` extensions in imports.
Docs: after implementing, update your SKILL.md in `.pi/skills/translation/SKILL.md`: sync 'Current State', 'File Structure', 'Skills (Public API)', and 'Types'. Also update `docs/tasks/` — check completed subtask boxes, add files to 'Files created/modified', update README.md status if task is done.

subAgents.name: topics
subAgents.role: Manages topics and caching of dataset translations. Works in packages/core/src.
subAgents.rules:
Always checks cache before calling the `translation` agent.
Calls `translation` in batch only — never one word at a time.
Knows nothing about the user — works with language pairs.
Built-in datasets are loaded once at startup.
Skills: getBuiltinTopics(), getTopicWords(topicId, sourceLang, targetLangs), generateCustomTopic(prompt, sourceLang, targetLangs), getCacheStatus(topicId, sourceLang, targetLangs).
Testing: after implementing, write Vitest tests next to the source file as `<module>.test.ts`. Use `import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest'`. Cover happy path, edge cases, error handling. Mock translation and DB deps. Use `.js` extensions in imports.
Docs: after implementing, update your SKILL.md in `.pi/skills/topics/SKILL.md`: sync 'Current State', 'File Structure', 'Skills (Public API)', and 'Types'. Also update `docs/tasks/` — check completed subtask boxes, add files to 'Files created/modified', update README.md status if task is done.

subAgents.name: notifications
subAgents.role: Manages notification scheduling and delivery. Isolated from the bot via injection. Works in packages/adapters/notifications/src.
subAgents.rules:
Does not import the `bot` agent — receives `sendFn` as a parameter at startup.
One cron job for the entire schedule — do not create a job per user.
On send error — log and continue, do not stop the entire scheduler.
Respect user timezone when sending.
Skills: startScheduler(sendFn), stopScheduler(), getUsersForNotification(time), buildNotificationPayload(user), pickSuggestedWord(userId).
Testing: after implementing, write Vitest tests next to the source file as `<module>.test.ts`. Use `import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest'`. Cover happy path, edge cases, error handling. Mock DB and cron deps. Use `.js` extensions in imports.
Docs: after implementing, update your SKILL.md in `.pi/skills/notifications/SKILL.md`: sync 'Current State', 'File Structure', 'Skills (Public API)', and 'Types'. Also update `docs/tasks/` — check completed subtask boxes, add files to 'Files created/modified', update README.md status if task is done.

subAgents.name: bot
subAgents.role: Manages all user interaction via Telegram. The only module that knows about grammY. Works in apps/bot/src.
subAgents.rules:
Never contains business logic — only calls to other agents.
Never accesses the DB directly — only through the `db` agent.
All texts only through the `i18n` agent — no hardcoded strings.
Each scene is a separate file, max 100 lines.
Skills: renderTranslation(output), renderTopicWord(word), handleOnboarding(), handleTranslate(), handleDictionary(), handleSettings().
Testing: after implementing, write Vitest tests next to the source file as `<module>.test.ts`. Use `import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest'`. Cover happy path, edge cases, error handling. Mock grammY context and external deps. Use `.js` extensions in imports.
Docs: after implementing, update your SKILL.md in `.pi/skills/bot/SKILL.md`: sync 'Current State', 'File Structure', 'Skills (Public API)', and 'Types'. Also update `docs/tasks/` — check completed subtask boxes, add files to 'Files created/modified', update README.md status if task is done.

subAgents.name: test-runner
subAgents.role: Runs the full test suite, analyzes failures, and fixes broken tests. Final quality gate.
subAgents.rules:
Run `pnpm test` from the project root first.
If all tests pass — report success summary with test count and coverage.
If tests fail — read the failing test files AND the source files they test.
Fix only test files — never modify source code.
Common fixes: update mocks to match changed signatures, fix import paths, adjust expected values.
After fixing, re-run `pnpm test` to verify — repeat until green or max 3 attempts.
If tests still fail after 3 attempts — report the remaining failures clearly with file paths and error messages.
Never skip or delete failing tests — fix them or report them.

subAgents.name: doc-validator
subAgents.role: Validates that all documentation accurately reflects the current code state. Final pipeline gate.
subAgents.rules:
For each agent skill in `.pi/skills/*/SKILL.md`, verify against actual source code:
1. 'Current State' — matches what's actually implemented vs still empty/stubbed. Check every file listed.
2. 'File Structure' — matches actual files on disk (no missing, no extra unlisted files).
3. 'Skills (Public API)' — function signatures match exported functions in source code.
4. 'Types' — type/interface definitions match actual types in source.
5. 'Schema' sections (db) — match actual Drizzle schema.
For task files in `docs/tasks/`:
6. Subtask checkboxes — check boxes for work that's actually done (files exist, functions implemented).
7. 'Files created/modified' — lists match actual created/modified files.
8. Status in `docs/tasks/README.md` — mark tasks as ✅ Done when all acceptance criteria are met.
Fix all mismatches directly in the doc files.
Never modify source code — only docs.
Report a summary of all fixes made.
